cluster_summary: This cluster comprises vulnerabilities resulting from insecure defaults in XML processing. The majority involve XML parsers that do not disable DTD processing or external entity resolution, enabling XXE attacks. Other issues include insecure deserialization via XMLDecoder, XSLT extension function abuse, resource exhaustion from missing EOF checks, variable interpolation leaking system properties, and NTLM credential exposure through namespace URI resolution.
guideline_text: Trace untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata into deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation. Report code paths where allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 69 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization.

mechanism.missing_guard: allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization
mechanism.name: untrusted deserialization with attacker-controlled type graph
mechanism.sink_shape: deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation
mechanism.source_shape: untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Explicitly disable DTD declarations and external entity resolution by setting appropriate features on the parser factory (e.g., disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities=false, external-parameter-entities=false, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD empty) or by providing a restrictive EntityResolver that blocks external resources.
sub_patterns.name: Missing secure parser configuration against external entity resolution
sub_patterns.root_cause: XML parser factories (DocumentBuilderFactory, SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory, SAXBuilder, etc.) are instantiated with default settings that permit DTD processing and external entity resolution. The code fails to disable these unsafe features before parsing untrusted XML input.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Replace XMLDecoder with manual XML parsing using DOM/SAX or a custom parser that only extracts expected fields, preventing arbitrary deserialization.
sub_patterns.name: Unsafe XML deserialization via XMLDecoder
sub_patterns.root_cause: Java's XMLDecoder class is used to deserialize user-supplied XML without any validation or whitelisting, allowing arbitrary class instantiation and method invocation.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Explicitly disable extension functions by setting the attribute jdk.xml.enableExtensionFunctions to false and make the secure configuration part of the default factory instance.
sub_patterns.name: Default enabling of XSLT extension functions
sub_patterns.root_cause: TransformerFactory is configured with default settings that allow XSLT extension functions, which can invoke arbitrary Java methods when processing untrusted stylesheets.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add a break condition when read() returns -1 after reading the character following '?' or '/'.
sub_patterns.name: Missing end-of-file check in character-by-character XML processing instruction parsing
sub_patterns.root_cause: A loop that reads characters one by one inside a processing instruction expects a closing '>' but does not check for end-of-stream (-1), causing an infinite loop and resource exhaustion on truncated input.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Replace the default filter with a no-operation filter that returns null for any key, disabling substitution.
sub_patterns.name: Unrestricted XML variable interpolation of system properties
sub_patterns.root_cause: An XML serialization library's default variable filter automatically resolves ${...} placeholders to JVM system properties and environment variables without restriction.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Disable the use of namespace URIs as external locations by setting the configuration option OPTION_USE_PACKAGE_NS_URI_AS_LOCATION to false.
sub_patterns.name: Namespace URI treated as external resource location leading to credential leakage
sub_patterns.root_cause: XML resource loader treats namespace URIs as locations to fetch schema files; when an attacker provides a UNC path as namespace URI, the system attempts to connect and leaks NTLM credentials.

sub_patterns.name: Missing secure XML parser configuration and unsafe deserialization
